$description: Golden merge scenarios for packages/local-store (docs/LOCAL_MODE_PLAN.md §3.4). Steps: {on, at, op, ...} edits a device's note; {send, to} merges one device's state into another; {exchange: [a, b]} merges both ways; {snapshot, of} / {deliver, to} replays an old copy; {compact, at} drops tombstones every device has seen; {expect, on} checks the state (sum is the golden checksum of the canonical file). Every merge is also checked for commutativity, idempotence and absorption. Edit this through scripts/merge-scenarios.py.
rules: doc fields: last write wins by c
doc fields: causality first (a later edit wins even with an older clock)
concurrent title change: history version and notice
tags: add-wins OR-set
content: cv(A) >= cv(B) takes A
content: concurrent, newer c wins, loser to history, cv = max
content: concurrent identical edits lose nothing
delete counts as a content write (delete vs edit)
position: last write wins on (parentId, rank), no notice
collapsed: last write wins, no notice
files, fileText, versionNames, collections, row values: last write wins per key
notices: union, dismissal last write wins
seen: pointwise max
permanent delete: the stub drops only edits it has seen
permanent delete: an unseen edit brings the note back in Trash with a restored notice
after merge: a missing or deleted parent moves the block to the top level
after merge: a cycle from concurrent moves is re-rooted at the block moved last
after merge: ranks tie-break by (rank, id)
compacted tombstones stay gone (a stale copy can't bring them back)
stale copies and duplicates change nothing
three-way concurrency converges
clock skew only changes which concurrent edit wins, never whether one is kept
